newsitem.title: UK: UK shares finish higher as U.S. rally continues.
newsitem.headline: UK shares finish higher as U.S. rally continues.

text.p: ** UK's FTSE closes higher but off day's best levels, helped
by company results and return of bid speculation.
** Dow puts on 22 points by London close.
** Gilts end weaker after stronger than expected UK RPI.
** Chubb ends sharply higher, says in bid talks.
But it was gains in U.S. shares that inspired the initial advance in response to the Dow's 100-point rally overnight and a close above 6,900 points for the first time.
"We tend to react to Wall Street in the morning now rather than at night because we don't believe it will finish where we left it," one dealer said, commenting on the U.S. stock market's volatility.

"We can easily ignore 50-point moves on the Dow, but we haven't yet got to the stage of ignoring 100-point moves," said another trader. The Dow was up another 22 points as London markets closed today after favourable U.S. economic data.

Domestic Retail Price Index (RPI) data was slightly less encouraging, showing that UK inflation rose by more than most economists were expecting. But a near-term interest rate rise to fight off inflationary pressures was still seen as extremely unlikely given the proximity to a general election.
An election must be held in Britain before the end of May.

"The data today suggests that the economy is doing nothing other than growing above trend," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon. "If the election is put off until May, I see it becoming increasingly more uncomfortable for the chancellor."
Gilts finished weaker on the day as investors fretted over rising inflation and the prospect of an early election also helped to drag the market lower.

Among individual share movers Chubb took centre stage and was one of the day's best performing stocks after the security firm said it was in talks that might lead to a recommended offer of up to 450p per share.
Shares in Chubb Security finished 82p higher at 423p.
Shell also stormed higher to end 26p better at 10.87-1/2 stg after announcing favourable annual results plus a stock split.

Shares in Pearson Plc fell 12-1/2p to 751p after the media group said it had discovered accounting irregularities. Improper accounting at Penguin USA could lead to a charge of as much as 100 million stg, Pearson said.
Mercury Asset Management Plc was also among the day's losers as the market interpreted the fund manager's move to raise a standby loan as a deterrent to predators.
The shares sank 39-1/2p to 13.29 stg as bid hopes faded.
Elsewhere some utility stocks suffered on reports that a windfall tax planned by the opposition Labour Party was legal. The Conservatives had said such a tax might breach EU laws.
-- Elaine Hardcastle, London newsroom +44 171 542 4027
